activity.title: Carry It Together
activity.goal: Move in step with a partner to carry something together.

steps.caption: Two corners for you, two for me.
Teddy is home! Swap and go again.

activity.safety: Clear the floor first, and walk, never run. Carry the towel low. Only a soft toy on the towel, nothing heavy. If there is an accident, call your local emergency number.
activity.forAdult: In the story, Maya and Amir find that taking turns works better than pulling. Carrying something together is the next step: two people have to watch each other and move at the same time. Lay a soft toy in the middle of a towel. You hold two corners and the child holds the other two. Say “Lift… together!” and walk slowly across the room to a “home”, such as a mat or a cushion, watching each other as you go. If the toy falls off, laugh, put it back and try again: that is part of the game. Then swap who walks in front. To make it easier, carry it only a few steps. To make it harder, walk round a chair on the way, or let two children carry it while you watch. Five to ten minutes is plenty.
activity.inClass: Children work in pairs, with one towel and one soft toy per pair: one adult with up to four children. Each pair carries its toy to a “home” mat and back, then the pair swaps who leads. The other pair cheers: “Together!”
